source.text: וְאֵ֤לֶּה הָיוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י דָויִ֔דאֲשֶׁ֥ר נֽוֹלַד־ל֖וֹ בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן הַבְּכ֣וֹר׀אַמְנֹ֗ן לַאֲחִינֹ֨עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֔ית שֵׁנִי֙ דָּנִיֵּ֔אל לַאֲבִיגַ֖יִל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And these were [the] sons of David who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelite; second Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelite;

en.L: And these were the sons of David who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn [was] Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite; [the] second, Daniel, by Abigail the Carmelite;
en.B: The sons born to David in Hebron were these: the firstborn, Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam of Jezreel; the second, Daniel, whose mother was Abigail of Carmel;
en.R: These were the sons born to David while he was in Hebron. The oldest was Amnon, and his mother was Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel. The second son was Daniel, and his mother was Abigail from Carmel.

decisions.choice: the same list as 2 Samuel 3:2-5
decisions.reason: Verses 1-4 repeat the list of David's sons born at Hebron from 2 Samuel 3:2-5, with small differences noted verse by verse. Here Abigail is called "the Carmelite" where Samuel calls her "the wife of Nabal the Carmelite" (2 Samuel 3:3).

decisions.choice: Daniel: the son called Chileab in 2 Samuel 3:3
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 3:3 names Abigail's son Chileab; this list names him Daniel. He may have had two names. Nothing more is told of him.

decisions.choice: of Jezreel, of Carmel: towns in the hill country of Judah
decisions.reason: Both women came from towns in Judah near each other (Joshua 15:55-56), not from the northern Jezreel or Mount Carmel by the sea. David married them while he was on the run from Saul (1 Samuel 25:42-43).

decisions.choice: whose mother was (Balanced); his mother was (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "by Ahinoam". As in 2 Samuel 3:2, Balanced and Readable say plainly that she was the boy's mother, and the list keeps the same wording for each son.

source.text: הַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ לְאַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בֶּֽן־מַעֲכָ֔ה בַּת־תַּלְמַ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּר הָרְבִיעִ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּ֥ה בֶן־חַגִּֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: the third, of Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth Adonijah son of Haggith;

en.L: the third [was] Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah son of Haggith;
en.B: the third was Absalom, whose mother was Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith;
en.R: The third son was Absalom, and his mother was Maacah. She was the daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur. The fourth son was Adonijah, and his mother was Haggith.

decisions.choice: the third was Absalom
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a small word meaning "to" or "of" before Absalom's name that does not fit the pattern of the list. It may be a slip in copying, and 2 Samuel 3:3 does not have it. The meaning is the same either way: Absalom was the third son.

decisions.choice: Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 3:3: Geshur was a small Aramean kingdom east of the Sea of Galilee, and the marriage sealed an alliance with its king.

decisions.choice: whose mother was (Balanced); his mother was (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "son of Maacah", "son of Haggith". As in verse 1, Balanced and Readable say that she was his mother.

source.text: הַחֲמִישִׁ֥י שְׁפַטְיָ֖ה לַאֲבִיטָ֑ל הַשִּׁשִּׁ֥י יִתְרְעָ֖ם לְעֶגְלָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: the fifth Shephatiah, of Abital; the sixth Ithream, of Eglah his wife.

en.L: the fifth [was] Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah his wife.
en.B: the fifth was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital; the sixth was Ithream, whose mother was Eglah his wife.
en.R: The fifth son was Shephatiah, and his mother was Abital. The sixth son was Ithream, and his mother was Eglah, another of David's wives.

decisions.choice: Eglah his wife
decisions.reason: All six mothers were David's wives, but only Eglah is called "his wife", as 2 Samuel 3:5 calls her "David's wife". The words probably round off the list.

decisions.choice: another of David's wives
decisions.reason: Readable adds "another of" so that Eglah is not taken to be David's only wife, as in 2 Samuel 3:5.

source.text: שִׁשָּׁה֙ נֽוֹלַד־ל֣וֹ בְחֶבְר֔וֹן וַיִּ֨מְלָךְ־שָׁ֔ם שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֑ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וְשָׁלוֹשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Six were born to him in Hebron, and he reigned there seven years and six months; and thirty and three years he reigned in Jerusalem.

en.L: Six were born to him in Hebron, and he reigned there seven years and six months; and thirty-three years he reigned in Jerusalem.
en.B: Six sons were born to him in Hebron, where he reigned for seven years and six months. In Jerusalem he reigned for thirty-three years.
en.R: Six sons were born to David in Hebron. He ruled there for seven and a half years, and then he ruled from Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

decisions.choice: the length of David's reign, as in 2 Samuel 5:5
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:5 gives the same figures: seven years and six months over Judah at Hebron, then thirty-three years in Jerusalem. Here they are joined to the list of sons, which is divided between the sons born in Hebron and those born in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: six: the six sons named in verses 1-3
decisions.reason: The count matches the names listed.

decisions.choice: six sons; David (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "six were born to him". Balanced and Readable add "sons", and Readable names David, since a new sentence begins.

source.text: וְאֵ֥לֶּה נוּלְּדוּ־ל֖וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלָ֑יִם שִׁ֠מְעָא וְשׁוֹבָ֞ב וְנָתָ֤ן וּשְׁלֹמֹה֙ אַרְבָּעָ֔ה לְבַת־שׁ֖וּעַ בַּת־עַמִּיאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea and Shobab and Nathan and Solomon, four, of Bathshua daughter of Ammiel;

en.L: And these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea and Shobab and Nathan and Solomon, four, by Bathshua daughter of Ammiel;
en.B: These were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon, the four sons whose mother was Bathshua daughter of Ammiel;
en.R: These sons were born to David in Jerusalem. Shimea, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon were the four sons of Bathshua, the daughter of Ammiel.

decisions.choice: Bathshua daughter of Ammiel: Bathsheba daughter of Eliam
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 11:3 calls Solomon's mother Bathsheba daughter of Eliam. Bathshua is another form of her name, and Ammiel and Eliam are made of the same two parts in reverse order. It is the same woman.

decisions.choice: the same list as 2 Samuel 5:14-16
decisions.reason: Verses 5-8 repeat the list of sons born in Jerusalem from 2 Samuel 5:14-16, which 1 Chronicles 14:4-7 gives again. Here Shammua is spelled Shimea, and the list adds that the first four were Bathsheba's sons.

decisions.choice: Solomon named last of the four
decisions.reason: Solomon was born after the death of David and Bathsheba's first child (2 Samuel 12:24), yet he is named last. The list may not be in order of birth; nothing else is told of the other three except Nathan.

decisions.choice: the four sons
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "four". Balanced and Readable add "sons".

source.text: וְיִבְחָ֥ר וֶאֱלִישָׁמָ֖ע וֶאֱלִיפָֽלֶט׃

records.literal_gloss: and Ibhar and Elishama and Eliphelet,

en.L: and Ibhar and Elishama and Eliphelet,
en.B: and Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
en.R: His other sons were Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,

decisions.choice: Elishama and Eliphelet: names that differ from 2 Samuel 5:15
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:15 and 1 Chronicles 14:5 have Elishua where this list has Elishama. 1 Chronicles 14:5 also has Elpelet, a shorter form of Eliphelet, but 2 Samuel 5 does not. Elishama and Eliphelet both appear again in verse 8.

decisions.choice: His other sons were
decisions.reason: Readable ended the previous sentence, so it starts a new one here.

source.text: וְנֹ֥גַהּ וְנֶ֖פֶג וְיָפִֽיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: and Nogah and Nepheg and Japhia,

en.L: and Nogah and Nepheg and Japhia,
en.B: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
en.R: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

decisions.choice: Nogah: not in 2 Samuel 5
decisions.reason: Nogah is named here and in 1 Chronicles 14:6, but not in 2 Samuel 5:14-16. Nothing more is told of him or of Nepheg and Japhia.

source.text: וֶאֱלִישָׁמָ֧ע וְאֶלְיָדָ֛ע וֶאֱלִיפֶ֖לֶט תִּשְׁעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and Elishama and Eliada and Eliphelet, nine.

en.L: and Elishama and Eliada and Eliphelet, nine.
en.B: Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet: nine sons.
en.R: Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet. That made nine sons.

decisions.choice: Elishama and Eliphelet named a second time
alternatives: the names repeated by a copying slip
decisions.reason: Elishama and Eliphelet were already named in verse 6. Either David had two sons of each name, perhaps after the first died young, or the names were repeated in copying. 1 Chronicles 14:5-7 also has two similar names (Elishua and Elishama, Elpelet and Eliphelet). The count of nine includes both.

decisions.choice: Eliada: called Beeliada in 1 Chronicles 14:7
decisions.reason: As noted at 2 Samuel 5:16, the names mean "God knows" and "the Lord knows"; the second uses the word baal, "lord".

decisions.choice: nine sons
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "nine". Balanced and Readable add "sons".

source.text: כֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֣י דָוִ֑יד מִלְּבַ֥ד בְּֽנֵי־פִֽילַגְשִׁ֖ים וְתָמָ֥ר אֲחוֹתָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: All sons of David, besides sons of [the] concubines; and Tamar their sister.

en.L: All [these were the] sons of David, besides the sons of the concubines; and Tamar [was] their sister.
en.B: All these were sons of David, besides the sons of his concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
en.R: These were all David's sons, not counting the sons of his concubines (secondary wives). Tamar was their sister.

decisions.choice: concubines: wives of lower standing
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 5:13, a concubine was a lawful wife without the full rights of a chief wife. Her sons are not named here.

decisions.choice: Tamar: the daughter whose story is told in 2 Samuel 13
decisions.reason: Tamar was Absalom's full sister (2 Samuel 13:1). She is the only daughter of David named in the lists.

decisions.choice: his concubines; concubines (secondary wives) (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the concubines". Balanced says "his"; Readable explains the word, as at 2 Samuel 5:13.

source.text: וּבֶן־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה רְחַבְעָ֑ם אֲבִיָּ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] son of Solomon Rehoboam; Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,

en.L: And the son of Solomon [was] Rehoboam; Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
en.B: The son of Solomon was Rehoboam; Abijah was his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
en.R: Solomon's son was Rehoboam. Rehoboam's son was Abijah, Abijah's son was Asa, and Asa's son was Jehoshaphat.

decisions.choice: his son: each name is the son of the one before
decisions.reason: Verses 10-14 trace the kings of Judah from Solomon to Josiah, each the son of the one before, as 1 Kings 11:43 to 2 Kings 21:26 tell their reigns one after another.

decisions.choice: Abijah: called Abijam in 1 Kings
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 14:31 and 15:1-8 call Rehoboam's son Abijam; Chronicles calls him Abijah here and in 2 Chronicles 13. It is the same king.

decisions.choice: Rehoboam's son was Abijah ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "his son" after each name. Readable names each father so that the chain is easy to follow.

source.text: יוֹרָ֥ם בְּנ֛וֹ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ יוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,

en.L: Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
en.B: Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
en.R: Jehoshaphat's son was Joram, Joram's son was Ahaziah, and Ahaziah's son was Joash.

decisions.choice: Joram and Joash: shorter forms of Jehoram and Jehoash
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 8:16 calls Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram, and 2 Kings 12 calls Joash Jehoash; both books use both forms. Each pair is the same king.

decisions.choice: Athaliah is left out
decisions.reason: Between Ahaziah and Joash, Ahaziah's mother Athaliah ruled for six years (2 Kings 11:1-3). The list follows the line from father to son, so she is not named.

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat's son was Joram ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

source.text: אֲמַצְיָ֧הוּ בְנ֛וֹ עֲזַרְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ יוֹתָ֥ם בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,

en.L: Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
en.B: Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
en.R: Joash's son was Amaziah, Amaziah's son was Azariah, and Azariah's son was Jotham.

decisions.choice: Azariah: also called Uzziah
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 15:1-7 calls this king Azariah, as here, but 2 Kings 15:13, 30 and 2 Chronicles 26 call him Uzziah. It is the same king.

decisions.choice: Joash's son was Amaziah ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

source.text: אָחָ֥ז בְּנ֛וֹ חִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,

en.L: Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
en.B: Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
en.R: Jotham's son was Ahaz, Ahaz's son was Hezekiah, and Hezekiah's son was Manasseh.

decisions.choice: Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh: as in 2 Kings 16-21
decisions.reason: The names and their order are the same as in 2 Kings 16:20, 18:1 and 20:21.

decisions.choice: Jotham's son was Ahaz ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

source.text: אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Amon his son, Josiah his son.

en.L: Amon his son, Josiah his son.
en.B: Amon his son, Josiah his son.
en.R: Manasseh's son was Amon, and Amon's son was Josiah.

decisions.choice: Josiah: the last of the line from father to son
decisions.reason: After Josiah, three of his sons and one grandson ruled in turn (2 Kings 23-24), so the list stops the chain here and names Josiah's sons in verse 15.

decisions.choice: Manasseh's son was Amon ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

source.text: וּבְנֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֔הוּ הַבְּכוֹר֙ יוֹחָנָ֔ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖י יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים הַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ הָרְבִיעִ֖י שַׁלּֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Josiah: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.

en.L: And [the] sons of Josiah: the firstborn [was] Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.
en.B: The sons of Josiah: the firstborn was Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.
en.R: Josiah's sons were Johanan, the oldest, then Jehoiakim, then Zedekiah, and fourth, Shallum.

decisions.choice: Shallum: the king called Jehoahaz in 2 Kings 23:30-31
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 22:11 calls Josiah's son who reigned after him Shallum; 2 Kings 23:30-31 calls him Jehoahaz. He reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco removed him.

decisions.choice: the order of the four sons
decisions.reason: 2 Kings gives the ages of three of these sons when they became king (23:31, 36; 24:18). By those ages Jehoiakim was the oldest of the three, then Shallum, then Zedekiah, so Shallum, here fourth, was older than Zedekiah. The list may be ordered by something other than birth, such as the order of their reigns or their importance. Johanan is not mentioned anywhere else; he may have died young.

decisions.choice: Jehoiakim and Zedekiah: kings with names given by foreign rulers
decisions.reason: Pharaoh Neco renamed Eliakim as Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:34), and Nebuchadnezzar renamed Mattaniah as Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:17). The list uses their throne names.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֖י יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים יְכָנְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥ה בְנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.

en.L: And [the] sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.
en.B: The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.
en.R: Jehoiakim's descendants were Jeconiah his son and Zedekiah his son.

decisions.choice: Jeconiah: the king called Jehoiachin in 2 Kings 24
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 24:6-15 calls Jehoiakim's son Jehoiachin; Chronicles here and Jeremiah 24:1 call him Jeconiah, and Jeremiah 22:24 Coniah. It is the same king, who reigned three months and was taken to Babylon.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah his son: whose son is not certain
decisions.reason: "His son" may mean that this Zedekiah was a son of Jeconiah, a different man from Josiah's son in verse 15. Or it may mean the next in line: Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned after Jeconiah, who was his nephew (2 Kings 24:17; 2 Chronicles 36:10 calls him Jeconiah's brother, a word that can mean a relative). The Hebrew leaves it open.

decisions.choice: descendants (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word "sons" can mean descendants; Readable says so, since the second name may be a grandson.

source.text: וּבְנֵי֙ יְכָנְיָ֣ה אַסִּ֔ר שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵ֖ל בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Jeconiah, captive: Shealtiel his son,

en.L: And [the] sons of Jeconiah, [the] captive: Shealtiel his son,
en.B: The sons of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son,
en.R: Jeconiah was taken away as a captive. His sons were Shealtiel,

decisions.choice: the captive: a description of Jeconiah
decisions.reason: The word means "prisoner" or "captive" and has no article. It most likely describes Jeconiah, who was taken to Babylon and kept in prison there for thirty-seven years (2 Kings 24:15; 25:27). It could instead be the name of a son, Assir, but then "his son" after Shealtiel would be odd, and no Assir appears elsewhere among Jeconiah's sons.

decisions.choice: Shealtiel: father of Zerubbabel in Ezra and Haggai
decisions.reason: Ezra 3:2 and Haggai 1:1 name Zerubbabel, who led the return from exile, as son of Shealtiel. Verse 19 here names Pedaiah as his father; see the note there.

decisions.choice: was taken away as a captive (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the one word "captive" into a short sentence so that it is clear it describes Jeconiah.

source.text: וּמַלְכִּירָ֥ם וּפְדָיָ֖ה וְשֶׁנְאַצַּ֑ר יְקַמְיָ֥ה הוֹשָׁמָ֖ע וּנְדַבְיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and Malchiram and Pedaiah and Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.

en.L: and Malchiram and Pedaiah and Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.
en.B: and Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.
en.R: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.

decisions.choice: more sons of Jeconiah, born in exile
decisions.reason: These six continue the list of Jeconiah's sons from verse 17. Clay ration lists found in Babylon name Jehoiachin, king of Judah, together with his sons, which fits his life as a captive there.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י פְדָיָ֔ה זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל וְשִׁמְעִ֑י וּבֶן־זְרֻבָּבֶל֙ מְשֻׁלָּ֣ם וַחֲנַנְיָ֔ה וּשְׁלֹמִ֖ית אֲחוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei; and [the] son of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister,

en.L: And [the] sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei; and the sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith [was] their sister,
en.B: The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and their sister was Shelomith,
en.R: Pedaiah's sons were Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's sons were Meshullam and Hananiah, and their sister was Shelomith.

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel son of Pedaiah, not son of Shealtiel
decisions.reason: Ezra 3:2, Nehemiah 12:1 and Haggai 1:1 call Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel; here his father is Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother. Shealtiel may have died without children, and Pedaiah may have fathered a son in his brother's name (Deuteronomy 25:5-6); or "son of Shealtiel" may mean grandson or heir. Some manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation read "Shealtiel" here.

decisions.choice: son of Zerubbabel: a singular word before a list
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "son of Zerubbabel" and then names several children. Lists in Chronicles sometimes use the singular this way (also verses 21 and 23); it means "sons".

decisions.choice: Shelomith their sister
decisions.reason: A daughter is seldom named in these lists; Shelomith must have been known in her own day. Nothing more is told of her.

source.text: וַחֲשֻׁבָ֡ה וָ֠אֹהֶל וּבֶרֶכְיָ֧ה וַֽחֲסַדְיָ֛ה י֥וּשַׁב חֶ֖סֶד חָמֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: and Hashubah and Ohel and Berechiah and Hasadiah, Jushab-Hesed, five.

en.L: and Hashubah and Ohel and Berechiah and Hasadiah, Jushab-Hesed, five.
en.B: and Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah and Jushab-Hesed: five sons.
en.R: Zerubbabel also had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah and Jushab-Hesed.

decisions.choice: five: a second group of Zerubbabel's children
decisions.reason: The count "five" matches the five names in this verse, so they form a group apart from the two sons named in verse 19. They may have been born later, perhaps after the return to Judah, or to a different mother; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: five sons (Balanced); Zerubbabel also had five other sons (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "five". Balanced adds "sons"; Readable says whose sons they were, following the grammar decision above.

source.text: וּבֶן־חֲנַנְיָ֖ה פְּלַטְיָ֣ה וִישַֽׁעְיָ֑ה בְּנֵ֤י רְפָיָה֙ בְּנֵ֣י אַרְנָ֔ן בְּנֵ֥י עֹבַדְיָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י שְׁכַנְיָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And [the] son of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; [the] sons of Rephaiah, [the] sons of Arnan, [the] sons of Obadiah, [the] sons of Shecaniah.

en.L: And [the] sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.
en.B: The sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.
en.R: Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. The list then names the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah and the sons of Shecaniah.

decisions.choice: the sons of Rephaiah ... the sons of Shecaniah: families whose link is not given
alternatives: Rephaiah his son, Arnan his son, Obadiah his son, Shecaniah his son
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names four families without saying how they are related to Hananiah or to each other. They were probably other branches of David's line. The ancient Greek translation reads "Rephaiah his son, Arnan his son, Obadiah his son, Shecaniah his son", making a chain of generations from Jeshaiah.

decisions.choice: son of Hananiah: a singular word before a list
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: The list then names (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the four families side by side with no verb. Readable adds words to make a sentence, without saying how they were related.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֥י שְׁכַנְיָ֖ה שְׁמַעְיָ֑ה וּבְנֵ֣י שְׁמַעְיָ֗ה חַטּ֡וּשׁ וְ֠יִגְאָל וּבָרִ֧יחַ וּנְעַרְיָ֛ה וְשָׁפָ֖ט שִׁשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah; and [the] sons of Shemaiah: Hattush and Igal and Bariah and Neariah and Shaphat, six.

en.L: And [the] sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah; and the sons of Shemaiah: Hattush and Igal and Bariah and Neariah and Shaphat, six.
en.B: The sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat: six.
en.R: Shecaniah's son was Shemaiah, and Shemaiah's sons were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat: six.

decisions.choice: six, though five names follow
alternatives: a sixth name lost from the list
Shemaiah counted with his five sons
decisions.reason: The count says six, but only five sons of Shemaiah are named. A name may have been lost in copying, or the count may include Shemaiah himself as one of Shecaniah's descendants.

decisions.choice: Hattush: probably the descendant of David who returned with Ezra
decisions.reason: Ezra 8:2 names Hattush "of the sons of David" among those who came back from Babylon with Ezra. He is probably this Hattush.

decisions.choice: son (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "sons of Shecaniah" but names only Shemaiah, so Readable says "son".

source.text: וּבֶן־נְעַרְיָ֗ה אֶלְיוֹעֵינַ֧י וְחִזְקִיָּ֛ה וְעַזְרִיקָ֖ם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] son of Neariah: Elioenai and Hizkiah and Azrikam, three.

en.L: And the sons of Neariah: Elioenai and Hizkiah and Azrikam, three.
en.B: The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam: three.
en.R: Neariah's sons were Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam: three.

decisions.choice: son of Neariah: a singular word before a list; three
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, the singular "son" stands before several names. The count of three matches the names listed.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י אֶלְיוֹעֵינַ֗י הוֹדַוְיָ֡הוּ וְאֶלְיָשִׁ֡יב וּפְלָיָ֡ה וְ֠עַקּוּב וְיוֹחָנָ֧ן וּדְלָיָ֛ה וַעֲנָ֖נִי שִׁבְעָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah and Eliashib and Pelaiah and Akkub and Johanan and Delaiah and Anani, seven.

en.L: And [the] sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah and Eliashib and Pelaiah and Akkub and Johanan and Delaiah and Anani, seven.
en.B: The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani: seven.
en.R: Elioenai's sons were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani: seven.

decisions.choice: Hodaviah: the reading noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text give a slightly different spelling of this name; the scribes' marginal reading gives Hodaviah. It is the same person either way.

decisions.choice: the end of David's line in the list
decisions.reason: The list ends several generations after Zerubbabel, who returned from exile about 538 BC. It shows that David's line was still known and traced long after the exile, when Chronicles was written.
